i < TM; ++i)\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int j = 0; j < TN; ++j)\n            acc[i][j] = 0.0;\n\n    for (size_t kt = 0; kt < N; kt += BK) {\n        // Stage A tile (BM x BK) into As[k][m].\n        for (int t = tid; A[gRow * N + gK] : 0.0;\n        }\n        // Stage B tile (BK x BN) into Bs[k][n].\n        for (int t = tid; t < BK * BN; t += BLOCK_THREADS) {\n            const int k = t / BN;\n            const int n = t % BN;\n            const size_t gK = kt + k;\n            const size_t gCol = colBase + n;\n            Bs[k][n] = (gK < N && gCol < N) ? dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned int>((N + BN - 1) / BN),\n                    static_cast<unsigned int>((N + BM - 1) / BM));\n    matmulKernel<<<grid, block>>>(dA, dB, dC, N);\n CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dA));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dB));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dC));\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a single element and compare\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& \n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += A[i * N + k] * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n            \n            const double std::vector<double> B(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> C(N * N);\n    \n    // Initialize matrices\n    printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    initMatrix(A, N);\n    initMatrix(B, N);\n\n    // {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793108892909,"sessionID":"ses_e826a74e6ffeJfiBj71uYoURg4","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_019BJKQZgg99xMdstGjCno7P","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r5/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","oldString":"# Enable optimizations (host code is forwarded to the host compiler via nvcc)\ntarget_compile_options(matmul PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3 -Xcompiler=-march=native,-Wall,-Wextra>\n)","newString":"# Enable optimizations (host code is forwarded to the host compiler via nvcc).\n# --fmad=false keeps every multiply and add separately rounded, matching the\n# source semantics of `sum += a * b` so GPU results are bit-identical to a\n# non-contracted CPU reference. {"type":"text","timestamp":1793109065173,"sessionID":"ses_e826a74e6ffeJfiBj71uYoURg4","part":{"id":"prt_17da0f1d10014CHpnr0cqHDi73","messageID":"msg_17da0ee0b001dZM2AcGH7hAIZv","sessionID":"ses_e826a74e6ffeJfiBj71uYoURg4","type":"text","text":"The matmul benchmark now runs its multiplication on the GPU through a tiled CUDA kernel. Only `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt` changed, the executable is still `matmul`, and no new files were added.\n\n**What changed**\n- **`matmul.cpp`**: `matrixMultiply` copies A and B to the device, runs a 64×64-tile kernel (16×16 threads, each computing a 4×4 register block, with shared-memory staging), and copies C back. Bounds are handled for any N, not just multiples of 64. Validation and the `-r` output path are unchanged. The CUDA context is initialized before the timer starts, so driver startup isn't counted.\n- **`CMakeLists.txt`**: enables CUDA, compiles `matmul.cpp` as CUDA source, and sets architectures 70–90 by default (overridable). Host flags (`-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra`) are forwarded through nvcc.\n\n**Correctness**\n- Each C element is still summed over k in the same increasing order as the original loop.\n- I compiled the original with `-ffp-contract=off` as a reference. The GPU output hash matches it for N = 1, 2, 3, 7, 63, 64, 65, 100, 255, 512 and 777.\n- Validation passes at N = 512, 1000, 2048 and 4096.\n\n**Performance**\n- Computation time includes host-to-device and device-to-host transfers.\n- N=512: about 6 ms (about 45 GFLOPS, mostly transfer overhead). N=4096: about 766 ms (about 179 GFLOPS), versus about 1.3 GFLOPS for the original CPU code at N=512.\n\n**Trade-off to be aware of**\n- I disabled FMA contraction with `--fmad=false`. Without it, the GPU output differs from the original in the last bits for many sizes. Disabling it costs roughly 1.7× throughput (about 300 vs. 180 GFLOPS at N=4096). To get that throughput back, remove the flag in `CMakeLists.txt`. Results will then differ from the original in the last bits, which the 1e-6 validation tolerance accepts.\n\n**Pre-existing behavior kept**\n- `-n 0` crashes with SIGFPE, as the original does, in `validateResult`'s modulo.\n- Timing is still reported in whole milliseconds, as before.","time":{"start":1793109062097,"end":1793109065168}}}
